docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The block diagram below shows the measuring subsystem for Team 206's pet feeder. It shows how the three light sensors, push buttons, LED, microcontroller pins, power levels, and team connection are arranged. The diagram will be updated with part numbers for design review.

docs.title: Power Source
docs.text: The subsystem is powered from 9 V, 1 A unregulated supply. The 9V supply feeds a voltage regulator that provides a regulated 5 V output for the subsystem.

docs.title: Power Levels
docs.text: The PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano, photoresistor, op-amp, pushbutton and LEDS are all on a 5 V rail. The 9 V rail is used as the input to the 5 V regulator.

docs.title: Sensors
docs.text: The subsystem uses three photoresistors to monitor the food level in the feeder. Photoresistor 1 detects the empty level, Photoresistor 2 detects the low-fill level, and Photoresistor 3 detects the high-fill level. Each sensor signal is conditioned by an op-amp circuit and then read by an ADC input on PIC18F57Q43.

docs.title: Actuators/ Outputs
docs.text: Two LEDS provide visual indication of the selected fill level. The microcontroller also provides digital output signal to the motor subsystem when filling should begin or stop based on the selected level and sensor reading.

docs.title: Component Selection
docs.text:
Table 1: Op Amp

Solution Pros Cons * Option 1.* MCP6004-I/P Quad Operational Amplifier* $0.60/each*Link to product * Operates on 5V* Four amplifiers in one* Low supply current (100 μA per amplifier)* Rail-to-rail inputs and outputs * Maximum Supply Voltage 6V needs regulation from 9V power source * Lower bandwidth (1 MHz) than the TL974IN (12 MHz)*Input offset voltage can introduce small measurements errors * Option 2. * TL974IN Quad Operational Amplifier * $1.66/each * Link to product * Works with 5V supply* Four amplifiers in one * Higher bandwidth(12 MHz) * More expensive * Higher power consumption *Limited input common mode voltage range * Option 3. * LM324N Quad Operational Amplifier * $0.58/each * Link to product * Operates on 5V* Four amplifiers in one * Inexpensive * Not rail-to-rail * Input common-mode range does not extend to the positive 5V supply rail *Higher input bias current (45nA) than the MCP6004 (1pA)

Choice: Option 1: MCP6004-I/P Quad Operational Amplifier

Rationale: The MCP6004 was selected becuase it can operate a 5V power supply and will have four Op Amps in one chip, which is enough for the three light sensors in our design. Its rail-to-rail input and output capability allows it to work with sinals close to the supply voltage. It also has low power consumption and is less expensive than option two.

Table 2: Light Sensor

Solution Pros Cons * Option 1.* PDV-P8103 CdS Photoresistor * $0.72/each*Link to product * Inexpensive* High dark resistance (500 kOhms minimum)* Resistance changes with light exposure * Requires a voltage-divider circuit * Lower minimum dark resistance than option 2*Ambient Lighting may affect readings * Option 2. * NSL-A95013 CdS Photoresistor * $0.88/each * Link to product * High minimum dark resistance (1.2 MOhms)* Resistance changes with light exposure * Good at detecting blocked light * More expensive than Option 1* requires a voltage divider circuit *Ambient lighting may affect readings * Option 3. * Adafruit 161 CdS Photoresistor * $0.95/each * Link to product * Simple design* Through hole installation * Detects changes in light when sensor is blocked * Most Expensive* Low Minimum dark resistance (200 kOhms) *Light resistance is not listed

Choice: Option 1: PDV-P8103 Photoresistor

Rationale: Option 1 was selected because of changing resistance when exposed to light allowing the system to detect when food blocks light at different levels of the container. It is affordable, uses through-hole mounting, and can be incorporated into a voltage divider circuit. Since our project uses three light sensors, its lower cost is also benefical.

Table 3: Voltage Regulator

Solution Pros Cons * Option 1.* NJM7805FA 5V Linear Voltage Regulator * $1.85/each*Link to product * Fixed 5V Output * Supports up to 1.5A * Through Hole Mounting * Most expensive*Lower maximum operating temperature (85 °C) *Less energy efficient than a switching regulator * Option 2. * MC7805ACTG 5V Linear Voltage Regultor * $1.07/each * Link to product * Fixed 5V output* Built-in overtemperature and short-circuit protection * Operating temperature up to 125°C *Lower rated output current (1A) * Produces heat when reducing 9V to 5V *Requires external capacitors for recommended operation * Option 3. * L7805ABV-DG 5V Linear Voltage Regulator * $1.53/each * Link to product * Fixed 5V output* Supports up to 1.5A * Overtemperature and short-circuit protection * More expensive than option 2* Produces heat when reducing 9V to 5V *Requires external capacitors for recommended operation

Choice: Option 3: L7805ABV-DG 5V Linear Voltage Regulator

Rationale: Option 3 provides a regulated 5V output needed for the circuit while accepting the 9V input from the power adapter. It includes overtemperature and short-circuit protection. Its 1A output rating matches our planned power requirements, provided the circuit's total current consumption stays within the limit

Table 4: 9V Power Supply

Solution Pros Cons * Option 1.* Adafruit 1448 Adjustable Power Adapter* $14.95/each*Link to product * Adjustable output voltage, including 9V * Include multiple connector tips * Can change between center-positive and center negative polarity * Most Expensive*Only supplies 900 mA at 9V,below the 1A requirment *Requires a different jack or connector adapter * Option 2. * GlobTek WR9HD1000LCP-F(R6B) * $10.35/each * Link to product * Fixed 9V output* Provides 1A output current * Less expensive than option 1 *5.5 x 2.5 mm plug does not match the PJ-102AH jack * Not adjustable to other voltages *Requires a different jack or connector adapter * Option 3. * GlobTekWR9HD1000CCP-F(R6B) * $10.35/each * Link to product * Fixed 9V output* Provides 1A output current * Less expensive than Option 1 * 5.5 x 2.1 mm plug compatiblity needs co* Not adjustable to other voltages*Limited to 1A output current

Choice: Option 3: GlobTek WR9HD1000CCP-F(R6B)

Rationale: The power adapter provides the required 9V and 1A output at a lower cost than the adjustable alternative. It also uses a North American wall plug and canter-positive polarity. Connector Compatibility will be verified before final assembly, and a compatible power jack can be selected if necessary.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This schematic represents the light sensor system for our automatic pet feeder. The design uses a PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano microcontroller to monitor three photoresistors that detect dfferent food levels. An op amp buffers the sensor signal before they reach the microcontroller. There is also two push buttons for selecting the desired fill level, two indicator LEDs, and an output that will be sent to the motor board and tell it when to activate and when to stop adding food. The board can be powered using a 9V DC input with a voltage regultor or an external regulated 5V supply. There are also additonal GPIO connections for testing and potential troubleshooting.
